currentContext.strategies: Convert revenue scale into profitability - management's stated key priority after FY26 saw revenue grow 23.58% while EBITDA margin fell 251 bps to 11.62% and PAT declined 4.19%|Drive operating leverage through technology: a new core backend platform, a direct web booking portal, strengthened customer and driver applications and integrations, with increasing automation and fewer manual processes over the next two years|Preserve the asset-light, vendor-owned fleet model (over 90% vendor-owned) to expand capacity and city coverage with low capital intensity, high ROCE (29.4%) and an effectively debt-free balance sheet|Deepen enterprise relationships and grow the blue-chip client base - 223 clients added in FY26 to over 1,750 active enterprises, with 55% of FY26 revenue from customers of more than five years|Extend international reach without owning a global fleet, through the SIXT partnership and a 30+ country network|Expand the operational network across India and international markets, including growth beyond metros into emerging cities|Institutionalise the company - strengthen leadership depth, governance and systems so that ECO Mobility becomes increasingly institution-driven as it enters its fourth decade|Seek expansion of current business operations as well as opportunities in adjacent and new areas
currentContext.expansion: ECOS expands by adding cities, vendor-partner fleet and platform capability rather than by building plants - the asset-light model, with more than 90% of the fleet vendor-owned, is explicitly described as enabling rapid expansion across cities while minimizing capital expenditure requirements. As on FY26 the operating footprint spanned 131 cities in India and more than 30 countries, run through a combination of owned offices and vendor partnerships, with a fleet network of over 20,000 vehicles (the Chairman's message refers to the FY26 network as over 19,000 vehicles, an internal inconsistency in the report). The Board's report states the Company expanded fleet capacity to over 20,000 vehicles during FY26 to support growing enterprise demand across 130+ cities in India. The other expansion axis is digital: continued investment in proprietary technology platforms, backend integration systems, fleet management tools and booking platforms, with a new core backend system implemented during FY26 to improve operational efficiency and customer experience, and increasing automation targeted as a source of operating leverage over the next two years. Management also identifies the movement of businesses, GCCs, manufacturing facilities and IT & ITES hubs into Tier II and Tier III cities as the geographic expansion opportunity for operators with nationwide reach. No plant, capacity-addition, commissioning or ramp-up programme is disclosed, and no rupee capex quantum is stated in the narrative chapters. The accounts do carry a 'Capital Commitments - for purchase of motor vehicles' note (pages 187 and 277), but the block supplied carries no dated period header and no printed unit, so its figures cannot be attributed to a period and are not usable.

risks.risk: Vendor dependency under the asset-light model
risks.note: More than 90% of the 20,000+ vehicle fleet is vendor-owned, so the company relies significantly on third-party vendor partners for fleet availability and service delivery. Any disruption in vendor relationships, shortage of vehicle availability, or inability to hold service-quality standards hits operational efficiency and customer experience directly - the flip side of the capital efficiency the model delivers.

The organized corporate mobility industry remains highly competitive with both organized and unorganized players, and management states increasing competition may impact pricing, margins, customer acquisition and market share. FY26 already shows the effect: profitability was hit partly by a change in customer mix toward clients on negotiated pricing and by competitive market conditions.

risks.risk: Margin compression - operating leverage not keeping pace with revenue growth
risks.note: Revenue grew 23.58% in FY26 but EBITDA rose only 1.7%, EBITDA margin fell 251 basis points to 11.62%, operating profit margin fell from 10.90% to 8.15% and net profit margin from 9.19% to 7.12%. Management attributes this to a one-time provision for bad and doubtful debts, higher employee benefit expense, negotiated-pricing customer mix and competition, and names improving operating leverage as a key priority - making margin recovery the central watch-item.

risks.risk: Receivables and credit quality in an enterprise-billing model
risks.note: FY26 profitability was impacted by a one-time and non-recurring provision for bad and doubtful debts. With revenue concentrated in corporate accounts billed in arrears (debtor turnover 8.52x), collection discipline is a structural exposure even though management describes collection efficiency as consistent.

risks.risk: Dependence on corporate spending and business-travel activity
risks.note: Demand is closely linked to overall economic activity, business travel trends and enterprise spending. Any slowdown in economic growth, reduced corporate travel, or lower outsourcing by enterprises directly reduces demand - a cyclical exposure with no captive or contracted backlog to cushion it.

risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance exposure across transport, tax, labour and safety law
risks.note: Operations are subject to various central and state regulations covering transportation, taxation, labour laws, environmental requirements and safety standards; changes in regulations, policies or compliance requirements could raise operating costs. Operating across 131 cities multiplies the number of state-level regimes to comply with.

As mobility operations become increasingly technology-driven, the company depends on robust digital infrastructure, data protection and uninterrupted platform performance. Cyber threats, technology disruptions, data breaches or system failures could adversely impact operations and customer confidence - heightened in FY26 by the implementation of a new core backend platform.

risks.risk: Operational and service-delivery execution at scale
risks.note: Operations involve large-scale coordination across multiple cities, customers, vendors and transport networks; operational inefficiencies, manpower challenges, traffic conditions, fuel price volatility or service interruptions may impact performance and customer satisfaction. The Board maintains a Risk Management Committee and an internal control and risk-mitigation system assessed through revised standard operating procedures.

one-line thesis: ECOS delivered strong volume growth (29% trips) and revenue expansion (23.6% FY26) driven by GCC demand and new client wins, but margins compressed to 11.6% due to strategic investments, one-off provisions, and competitive pricing in ETS. The outlook hinges on operating leverage kicking in as manpower cost growth moderates relative to revenue, with guidance targeting 18-20% revenue growth and 11-13% EBITDA margins for FY27.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 2,067.6M (Q4, +16.7% YoY), INR 8,081.6M (FY26, +23.6% YoY); EBITDA: INR 241.5M (Q4, -8.7% YoY), INR 939.3M (FY26, margin ~11.6% vs ~14% prior year); PAT: Impacted by INR 80M one-time doubtful debt provision and elevated employee costs (+42% YoY opex growth); Order Book: Not disclosed (contractual recurring revenue model); Net Debt: Net Cash position with INR 1,373M cash/investments; One-offs: INR 80M provision for doubtful debts (legal recovery ongoing).
guidance: Revenue Growth: 18-20% for FY27; EBITDA Margin: 11-13%; Order Inflow: 60-65% growth from new client acquisitions, rest from wallet share expansion; Capex: Maintained at ~INR 30M/year unless EV infrastructure matures; Commissioning: N/A (service model).
order book & pipeline: Recurring revenue model with 1,750+ active clients; 55% of revenue from clients >5 years; low churn (~2-3%) in top 200 accounts; 223 new clients added in FY26.
segment / subsidiary detail: ETS: 57-58% of revenue, stable IT/ITES demand, surge from GCCs, higher competitive pricing pressure; CCR: 42-43% of revenue, diversified demand, impacted briefly by West Asia crisis in March, 14% bookings via digital platforms.
growth verticals / optionality: Global expansion via SIXT partnership (100+ countries); Deepening penetration in GCCs and manufacturing hubs; Digital adoption (CabDrive Pro, web portal) to serve SMEs/premium individual users; Vendor consolidation trend among large enterprises.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 margin pressure from: 1) Higher manpower costs (hikes given, expected to moderate to 13-16% growth in FY27); 2) INR 80M one-time provision; 3) Competitive pricing in ETS reducing average ticket size; Fuel cost is largely pass-through with minor lag impact.
capex / expansion: Asset-light model; Fleet of 20,000 vehicles via vendor partners; Minimal owned capex (~INR 30M/year avg); Cautious on EV capex due to immature product reliability and charging infrastructure concerns.
capital allocation: Strong balance sheet with INR 1,373M cash; Focus on organic growth and tech enablement; Dividend deferred pending separate board discussion; No M&A disclosed.
risks & watch-items: Competitive pricing wars from new entrants in ETS; Fuel price volatility (though pass-through exists); Geopolitical tensions impacting CCR (West Asia); Slow adoption of EVs limiting sustainability narrative; Execution risk in scaling leadership bandwidth.
management quality / tone: Pragmatic and disciplined; Acknowledges margin compression as a phase of investment; Confident in long-term structural shift to organized players; Cautious on EV hype; Emphasizes 'right to win' via service consistency over price.
non-obvious takeaways: Average revenue per trip is declining (INR 1,750 in FY24 to INR 1,550 in FY26) not just due to pricing but due to mix shift towards shorter ETS trips and airport transfers; 14% digital booking penetration in CCR is a leading indicator of stickiness and cost efficiency despite corporate preference for email booking.

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: One of India's leading providers of chauffeur-driven corporate mobility, offering Chauffeured Car Rentals and Employee Transportation Services to enterprise customers across 131 cities in India through a technology-enabled, predominantly asset-light model.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: ECOS (India) Mobility & Hospitality Limited provides chauffeur-driven mobility solutions to corporate customers through two verticals - Chauffeured Car Rentals (CCR) for executive transport, airport transfers, conferences and business meetings, and Employee Transportation Services (ETS) for 24x7 workforce commute with route optimisation and tracking. It also offers integrated corporate mobility management across multiple cities, dedicated event transportation and cross-border mobility coordination. Customers are corporates, MNCs, GCCs, IT & ITeS and manufacturing companies, institutions, event managers and B2B2C travel, served by professionally trained chauffeurs on a fleet network that is over 90% vendor-owned.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Chauffeured Car Rentals (CCR):** Executive transport, Airport transfers, Conference and business-meeting travel, Institutional travel
- **Employee Transportation Services (ETS):** 24x7 workforce commute with route optimization & tracking, Shift-based customised employee transportation
- **Corporate Mobility Solutions:** Integrated end-to-end mobility management across multiple cities
- **Event Transportation:** Dedicated fleet coordination for corporate events, delegations
- **Global Mobility Coordination:** Cross-border travel & mobility facilitation in 30+ countries, SIXT global network partnership

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Recurring revenue model with 1,750+ active clients; 55% of revenue from clients >5 years; low churn (~2-3%) in top 200 accounts; 223 new clients added in FY26.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: 18-20% for FY27; EBITDA Margin: 11-13%; Order Inflow: 60-65% growth from new client acquisitions, rest from wallet share expansion; Capex: Maintained at ~INR 30M/year unless EV infrastructure matures; Commissioning: N/A (service model).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Global expansion via SIXT partnership (100+ countries); Deepening penetration in GCCs and manufacturing hubs; Digital adoption (CabDrive Pro, web portal) to serve SMEs/premium individual users; Vendor consolidation trend among large enterprises.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural shift from fragmented, unorganized local transport operators to organized mobility providers offering standardized quality, nationwide coverage, compliance and technology integration - accelerating formalization of the industry
- Rapid expansion of India's GCC ecosystem: India hosts more than 1,700 GCCs with over 170 new GCCs established in CY2025; the market, put at ~USD 69.85 billion in 2025, is expected to reach nearly USD 130.5 billion by 2033 (~8.1% CAGR), driving sustained demand for employee transportation, chauffeur-driven rentals and airport transfers
- Enterprise focus on employee safety and operational transparency - demand for real-time tracking, route monitoring, centralized command, driver verification and SOS features, especially from MNCs, IT & ITES companies and GCCs running round-the-clock transport
- Rapid digital transformation of the industry - investment in transportation management systems, route optimization, automation platforms, analytics and real-time fleet monitoring improves utilisation, turnaround time and customer experience
- Expansion of businesses, GCCs, manufacturing facilities and IT & ITES hubs into Tier II and Tier III cities, favouring operators with scalable networks and nationwide reach
- Rising demand for single-vendor integrated mobility platforms covering ETS, chauffeur-driven rentals, airport transfers, event transport, centralized reporting and billing integration
- Growth in premium and executive transportation as MNC presence, GCC expansion and executive travel increase demand for high-quality chauffeur-driven services
- Macro backdrop: India's real GDP grew 7.6% in FY2025-26 and is projected by the IMF and RBI to grow approximately 6.6% in FY2026-27, with resilient domestic demand, infrastructure investment and structural reforms; inflation broadly within the RBI's target range and the repo rate at approximately 5.25%
- Company-level demand evidence in FY26: trips up nearly 29% to 5.23 million, revenue growth driven by higher trip volumes, new enterprise client additions, expanded mobility requirements from existing customers and increasing demand from GCC-led sectors
- Margin watch-items flagged: FY26 profitability was hit by a one-time provision for bad and doubtful debts, higher employee benefit expense, a customer-mix change toward enterprise clients on negotiated pricing, and competitive market conditions
- Risk-side drivers: high competitive intensity from organized and unorganized players, dependence on corporate spending and business-travel activity, vendor dependency under the asset-light model, and technology/cybersecurity exposure

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: FY26 margin pressure from: 1) Higher manpower costs (hikes given, expected to moderate to 13-16% growth in FY27); 2) INR 80M one-time provision; 3) Competitive pricing in ETS reducing average ticket size; Fuel cost is largely pass-through with minor lag impact.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Strong balance sheet with INR 1,373M cash; Focus on organic growth and tech enablement; Dividend deferred pending separate board discussion; No M&A disclosed.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: ECOS expands by adding cities, vendor-partner fleet and platform capability rather than by building plants - the asset-light model, with more than 90% of the fleet vendor-owned, is explicitly described as enabling rapid expansion across cities while minimizing capital expenditure requirements. As on FY26 the operating footprint spanned 131 cities in India and more than 30 countries, run through a combination of owned offices and vendor partnerships, with a fleet network of over 20,000 vehicles (the Chairman's message refers to the FY26 network as over 19,000 vehicles, an internal inconsistency in the report). The Board's report states the Company expanded fleet capacity to over 20,000 vehicles during FY26 to support growing enterprise demand across 130+ cities in India. The other expansion axis is digital: continued investment in proprietary technology platforms, backend integration systems, fleet management tools and booking platforms, with a new core backend system implemented during FY26 to improve operational efficiency and customer experience, and increasing automation targeted as a source of operating leverage over the next two years. Management also identifies the movement of businesses, GCCs, manufacturing facilities and IT & ITES hubs into Tier II and Tier III cities as the geographic expansion opportunity for operators with nationwide reach. No plant, capacity-addition, commissioning or ramp-up programme is disclosed, and no rupee capex quantum is stated in the narrative chapters. The accounts do carry a 'Capital Commitments - for purchase of motor vehicles' note (pages 187 and 277), but the block supplied carries no dated period header and no printed unit, so its figures cannot be attributed to a period and are not usable.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Pragmatic and disciplined; Acknowledges margin compression as a phase of investment; Confident in long-term structural shift to organized players; Cautious on EV hype; Emphasizes 'right to win' via service consistency over price.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Asset-light model: over 90% of the 20,000+ vehicle fleet is vendor-owned, enabling scalable expansion with low capital intensity and high return ratios (ROCE 29.36% in FY26)
- Pan-India operating footprint across 131 cities supported by owned offices and an extensive vendor partner network - nationwide single-vendor capability that fragmented local operators cannot match
- Technology-led operations: proprietary transportation management platform, new core backend system, direct web booking portal, customer and driver apps, real-time tracking and route optimisation
- Deep, sticky enterprise relationships - 55% of FY26 revenue came from customers of more than five years' standing; 223 new clients added during FY26
- Blue-chip customer franchise: 70+ Fortune 500 and 75+ BSE 500 companies among 1,750+ active corporate clients
- Over 30 years of industry experience (established 1996) and an experienced management team across mobility, operations, finance, HR and technology
- Effectively debt-free balance sheet (debt-equity 0.00 as on 31 March 2026) supporting growth without leverage
- Global reach without global fleet ownership through the SIXT partnership and a 30+ country network

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Competitive pricing wars from new entrants in ETS; Fuel price volatility (though pass-through exists); Geopolitical tensions impacting CCR (West Asia); Slow adoption of EVs limiting sustainability narrative; Execution risk in scaling leadership bandwidth.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Average revenue per trip is declining (INR 1,750 in FY24 to INR 1,550 in FY26) not just due to pricing but due to mix shift towards shorter ETS trips and airport transfers; 14% digital booking penetration in CCR is a leading indicator of stickiness and cost efficiency despite corporate preference for email booking.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Convert revenue scale into profitability - management's stated key priority after FY26 saw revenue grow 23.58% while EBITDA margin fell 251 bps to 11.62% and PAT declined 4.19%
- Drive operating leverage through technology: a new core backend platform, a direct web booking portal, strengthened customer and driver applications and integrations, with increasing automation and fewer manual processes over the next two years
- Preserve the asset-light, vendor-owned fleet model (over 90% vendor-owned) to expand capacity and city coverage with low capital intensity, high ROCE (29.4%) and an effectively …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising fuel prices and need for compliant, scalable mobility solutions for GCCs and large enterprises | ECOS (India) Mobility & Hospitality Ltd | beneficiary | High | Direct pass-through of fuel costs protects margins; asset-light model allows rapid scaling without capex burden; SIXT partnership opens high-margin international cross-sell opportunities. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Listing] The company got listed on NSE and BSE on 4th September 2024 (journey slide), and the historical-financials slide notes 'ECOs got listed in FY25'.
- [Partnership] Further progress reported on the SIXT partnership during Q1 FY27, alongside the launch of new technology for CCR.
- [Footprint contradiction] The company letterhead claims 'Providing Ground Transportation in 100+ Cities in India & 30+ Countries Worldwide', while the snapshot and business-overview slides state 151/151+ cities in India and 30+ countries worldwide.
- [Track record] Awards cited include Best Luxury Ground Handler (Today's Traveler, 2018), National Tourism Award for Luxury Car Tourist Transport Operator by GoI (FY14, FY15, FY16, FY17), Dun & Bradstreet SME Business Excellence Award (2017), and India's Best Employee Transportation Company (iNFHRA 2021).
